title: Laddered ranker head-to-head summary (Mar 2026)
body:
Quick summary

Purpose: run a laddered head-to-head ranking (staged pairwise comparisons) across three candidate variants to pick a model to promote to staging for conversational summarization workloads. This doc collects raw win/loss counts, sample slices where regressions appeared, and a pragmatic rollout recommendation.

Context and why this test:
- Prompt set: 1,200 prompts (mix: 40% customer-facing emails, 30% internal notes, 20% long-doc extract summarization, 10% low-resource languages). Prompts curated from prod prompt pool + handpicked edge cases from last quarter regressions.
- Metrics tracked: pairwise win-rate (human preference A/B), objective ROUGE-L, response latency p95 (ms), token-cost estimate (USD per 1k tokens), and regression-alert count (from eval harness).
- Candidates (short names used in results):
  - V_A: openlm-13b-v2-quant (int8 tuned, recent kernel optimizations)
  - V_B: redwood-rlhf-7b-v3 (smaller base, instruction-tuned aggressive decoding)
  - V_C: opt-30b-llm-slim (larger, looser decoding constraints, experimental safety filter)

Methodology notes (quick):
- Ladder procedure: initial seeding pairwise matches (A vs B, B vs C, A vs C) using disjoint prompt folds (400 prompts each). Winners advanced to final head-to-head on 600 holdout prompts. Human annotation: 3 raters per example, majority decides. Raters blind to model id.
- Statistical threshold: required >55% win-rate and p<0.05 (two-sided) to consider meaningful. For ties or near-threshold we also consulted ROUGE-L delta >0.5 and regression counts.
- Runtime conditions: all candidates served from the same dedicated cluster image; batching profile fixed to our staging baseline. Latency measured end-to-end.

Raw results (head-to-head aggregates):

Pairwise wins (human preference, majority):
- A vs B: A wins 62% (248/400)  | p<0.01  | ROUGE-L delta +1.2 favor A | reg alerts: A=6, B=13
- B vs C: B wins 54% (216/400)  | p=0.07  | ROUGE-L delta +0.3 favor B | reg alerts: B=13, C=9
- A vs C: A wins 59% (236/400)  | p=0.02  | ROUGE-L delta +0.9 favor A | reg alerts: A=6, C=9

Final decider (winner vs runner-up on 600 holdout prompts):
- A vs B (final): A wins 58% (348/600) | p=0.01 | ROUGE-L +0.8 | latency p95: A=540ms, B=420ms | cost est per 1k tokens: A=$3.20, B=$1.10

Interpretation notes:
- Quality: V_A shows consistent human-preference win over both V_B and V_C. ROUGE-L deltas align with preference direction.
- Cost/latency tradeoff: V_A is materially more expensive and slower (larger memory/quantization overhead) compared to V_B. V_B is faster and cheaper but loses on human preference by a non-trivial margin.
- Regression signal: majority of reg alerts for V_B are tied to hallucination on long-doc summarization slices and inconsistent attribution in email summarizations; V_A reg alerts are concentrated in low-resource language prompts (quality dipped there).

Win/loss breakdown by slice (top slices where differences matter):
- Long-doc summarization (350 prompts): A wins 66% vs B; B shows hallucination cases (confident wrong facts) ~5% of slice.
- Customer emails (480 prompts): A wins 55% vs B; B faster, but on aggressive instruction-following A produced more succinct, accurate action-items.
- Internal notes/short queries (240 prompts): B = A (roughly tied at 51% A).
- Low-resource languages (130 prompts): C and A both beat B; A has a small drop vs C on dialect variants.

Qualitative failure modes (examples appended in eval harness, see linked artifacts):
- B hallucination example (long-doc): model fabricates author statement when summarizing appendix. (Ticket JIRA-ML-4301)
- A low-resource drop: misses idiomatic particle in Bahasa prompt -> loses meaning (Ticket JIRA-ML-4320)

Decision recommendation (current):
- Promote V_A to staging for a limited canary (recommended) with staged rollout and safeguards:
  - Canary traffic: 5% of staging traffic for 48 hours, monitor user-facing eval set + production golden prompts.
  - Automatic rollback triggers: >3% absolute drop in human-preference score on live golden prompts OR >2x increase in regression-alert rate compared to baseline.
  - Additional slice gating: holdback V_A on low-resource-language region until we run small targeted fine-tuning pass or augment prompts.

Risk and mitigations:
- Latency/cost: V_A increases cost estimate ~2.9x for this workload. Mitigate by enabling prefix caching for repeated contexts and experimenting with mixed-precision (quant-iff safe) in a follow-up perf sprint. (See PR #341 for quant config options.)
- Regression on low-resource: run 1k-shot targeted eval and consider light fine-tune using anonymized corpora; coordinate with privacy and legal for data use.

Follow-up experiments (short backlog):
- Perf-experiment: run V_A with kernel-level async KV caching to try to reduce p95 by ~100ms. (Owner: Ethan)
- Fine-tune test: small in-domain low-resource adapt (200k tokens) for V_A to see if reg alerts drop. (Owner: Sofia)
- Cost-aware steady-state: simulate 10k qps mix to estimate monthly spend delta and evaluate autoscaling policy impact. (Owner: Ravi)

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Product: is the 2.9x cost multiplier acceptable for customers on staging? (flagging to PM: @James O'Neill)
- Privacy/legal: confirm allowed datasets for the suggested low-resource fine-tune.
- Ops: do we want to allocate dedicated GPU pool for V_A in staging or run on shared? (affects latency/cost).

Appendix: attachments and where to find raw outputs
- Raw human annotations CSVs: linked in Confluence page (see linked artifacts).
- Failure case sketches and annotator notes: folder /applied-ml/evals/laddered/mar-2026/failures
- Full per-example latency/cost trace: internal perf bucket (s3 link in Confluence).

TL;DR: V_A wins human preference and objective ROUGE head-to-head, but carries a sizeable latency and cost penalty and a small low-resource regression. Recommend limited staging promotion with 5% canary, strict rollback gates, and parallel mitigation work (perf + targeted fine-tune) before a wider rollout.

Notes to reviewers:
- Please scan the long-doc hallucination examples first (they are the most product-impactful).
- If you disagree with the decision threshold (55% win-rate), state the alternate threshold and reasons in comments below.
- Targets: Would like final decision by 2026-03-24 so we can schedule the canary for next sprint.
